qt: to the Commission Susanna Ceccardi (PfE), Anna Maria Cisint (PfE), António Tânger Corrêa (PfE), Silvia Sardone (PfE), Volker Schnurrbusch (ESN), Ondřej Knotek (PfE), Sebastian Tynkkynen (ECR), Isabella Tovaglieri (PfE), Seán Kelly (PPE) Subject:

Ending the seasonal clock changes represents an opportunity to make daily activities more predictable, to make better use of afternoon daylight and to support sectors such as tourism, retail, hospitality and leisure. Permanent summer time could contribute to these objectives, provided that its energy, health and economic impacts are assessed on the basis of up-to-date scientific evidence. In 2018, the Commission proposed ending seasonal clock changes, and in 2019, Parliament endorsed this objective. However, the absence of an agreement in the Council has prevented the legislative process from being completed. The Commission subsequently announced a new study on the effects of the reform, with results expected by the end of 2026. In the light of the above, the Commission is asked: 1.
When will the results of the study be published, and how does the Commission intend to involve Parliament in assessing its findings?
Is the Commission prepared to promote a legislative process to enable the adoption of permanent summer time, assessing its potential benefits and drawbacks on the basis of up-to-date data?

What initiatives does the Commission intend to undertake to facilitate an agreement among Member States, through the establishment of an implementation timetable, while safeguarding European coordination, protecting the functioning of the internal market and taking into account the needs of different regions?
